# nepal-payments

> Khalti, eSewa, ConnectIPS and Hamro Pay payments for Node.js and Next.js. One typed TypeScript API to start and verify payments from Nepal's gateways. Server only, Node 18+, zero runtime dependencies.

Start with `createPayments({ mode: 'sandbox' | 'live' | 'mock', khalti?, esewa?, connectips?, hamropay? })`. Each gateway client has `initiate`, `parseCallback`, `verify({ ref, expectedAmount, expectedOrderId })`, `status` (the gateway's report with no checks and no `paid` field; not for fulfilment), and (Khalti) `refund`. Amounts are integer paisa (`rupees(100)`). Check errors with `isPaymentError(e)`, not `instanceof`, and read `e.code`. Ship only when `verify(...).paid` is true. For eSewa, pass the signed callback to verify (`callback: cb`): the status API only echoes the amount you send. Khalti's lookup has no order id: store `start.ref` (the pidx) at initiate and verify only that stored pidx, never the pidx from the callback URL.

## Docs

- [Rules for coding agents](AGENTS.md): five rules for writing payment code with this package
- [Khalti](docs/khalti.md): redirect, lookup, statuses, refund
- [eSewa](docs/esewa.md): signed form, signed callback, status API, AMBIGUOUS
- [ConnectIPS](docs/connectips.md): RSA-signed form from a .pfx, validatetxn
- [Hamro Pay](docs/hamropay.md): session, signed form, webhook, transaction status
- [Express](docs/express.md): one-file recipe
- [Next.js App Router](docs/nextjs.md): Route Handlers on the Node.js runtime
- [NestJS](docs/nestjs.md): provider and controller
- [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md): socket and plugs, how to add a gateway

## Entry points

- `nepal-payments`: everything
- `nepal-payments/khalti`, `/esewa`, `/connectips`, `/hamropay`: one gateway each
- `nepal-payments/testing`: `fakeFetch` and fake gateway handlers (MSW-compatible) for tests
- `nepal-payments/compat`: the 2.x `NepPayments` class
